text:
Maya: sketching a midterm plan: 'tenant shaping' as a first-class routing primitive. idea is dynamic shaping rules per-tenant to control tail-cost and isolation without full tenancy splits.
Ravi: can you explain how shaping differs from current lanes/slices?
Maya: shaping = policy that adjusts concurrency, batch size, and model tier based on short-term metrics. unlike static lanes it's continuous and score-driven. low risk tenants get best-effort while noisy ones get gradual throttling.
Jordan: sounds useful. what about multi-region consistency? we can't have two regions making opposing shaping decisions for the same session.
Maya: agree. proposal: central policy engine holds canonical shaping state, zones subscribe. policy updates are monotonic and versioned; regional router applies latest version with session affinity tags.
Lee: operationally, how will customers see this? will API responses change?
Maya: no API surface change. we'll emit events to tenant telemetry stream and billing flags. opt-in via org settings first, then auto-profile for super-noisy tenants with manual override.
Ravi: rollout/launch criteria? we need concrete gates.
Maya: draft gates: 1) policy engine stress-tested at production QPS, 2) <1% increase in P99 for control group across regions, 3) per-tenant rollback via API within 10m, 4) CS notification events reach customers in <5m.
Jordan: add quality gate: model switch downgrade can't exceed 1.5% regression on customer eval prompts over 24h.
Lee: agree. also include security check: no KV cache cross-tenant exposure; shaping must zero out KV TTL if moving to degraded mode.
Maya: good catch. tech spec snippet:
```yaml
shaping_rule:
  priority: 50
  match:
    tenant_labels:
      - beta
  controls:
    concurrency_limit: 20
    preferred_batch: 8
    fallback_model: small-quant-v2
    kv_cache_ttl: 0s
  reevaluate_every: 300s
```
Ravi: metrics to monitor: per-tenant CPU/GPU utilization, request latency tails, batch sizes observed, kv-miss-rate, cross-region session handoffs.
Jordan: testing: unit policy decisions, chaos tests for policy propagation delay, and perf with synthetic noisy tenants causing cascading effects.
Lee: runbook items: how to pause shaping globally, how to forcibly pin a tenant to committed lane, how to purge KV for a tenant. keep instructions scripted.
ops-bot: alert: env-staging shaping-engine deployment started. link: https://deploys.internal/shaping-engine
Maya: stakeholder asks we've captured: 1) enterprises want explicit SLA carveouts, 2) platform teams want a way to tag tenants as 'never-shape', 3) billing needs shaped-usage breakdown.
Ravi: acceptance checklist (short): - central policy engine has HA and versioning - regional routers honor shaping within 2s of policy change - no >1% P99 regression on baseline - telemetry + billing signals exist - runbook + CS playbook documented.
Jordan: prioritization: MVP = central policy + regional subscriber + basic controls (concurrency, model fallback). Phase 2 = auto-profiling, tenant scoring, and UI in console.
Lee: estimate: MVP 6 weeks with small team (2 infra, 2 runtime, 1 product). Phase 2 an additional 8-10 weeks.
Maya: assigning: Ravi to draft policy API, Jordan to own tests & chaos, Lee to coordinate CS/billing hooks. I'll draft the spec doc and post in product channel for feedback.
Ravi: on it.
Jordan: will start test harness.
Lee: will scope CS notification format.
Maya: ending thread — will create formal PRD by Friday. Continue async here.
